title: JIT selection from independent streams: replace the big backlog with separate prioritized lists
summary: Jason Cohen argues that one big ordered backlog conflates prioritization (what is most important) with work-planning (what we do next), and forces comparison of incomparable things. His fix: keep separate prioritized lists per stakeholder group, customer journey stage or other category, then pick from the top of each list just in time when planning work.

principles.text: Prioritization (what is most important) is not work-planning (what we work on next); don't use one backlog for both.
principles.quote: Prioritization means: What is most important? Critically, it does not mean: What will we work on next?

principles.text: A single sorted list mixes incomparable kinds of importance (customer retention, competition, security, tech debt), so no one metric can order it.
principles.quote: The first problem is that you're sorting things that are incomparable.

principles.text: Have each stakeholder group (Sales, Support, Engineering) prioritize its own list, answering one question for just that group.
principles.quote: The solution is to prioritize items in separate, actually-comparable streams, and to keep that prioritization effort cleanly separate from work-planning.

principles.text: Forcing a group to rank its own ideas builds empathy for PM tradeoffs and prevents everything being Priority #1.
principles.quote: By forcing that group to prioritize their ideas, they'll argue amongst themselves over which are most impactful.

principles.text: Wait until the last moment to cross streams: pick the next work from the top of each list, then order it in a backlog.
principles.quote: By waiting until the last second to compare incomparable things, prioritization remains organized and clear.

principles.text: Selecting from the top items of each stream is easier, easier to explain to stakeholders, and lets you audit starvation and spot cross-stream wins.
principles.quote: It's a lot easier to pick the best from 12 instead of from 1000, and in some sense you can't go wrong
